If you don’t need to watch the browsers, run all agents in headless mode. Then window focus doesn’t matter and operations *really* run in parallel.

If multiple agents share one OS-level browser window or context, the OS will focus that one and make interactions appear serialized.

If you find shared state, fix it by:

- Avoiding static/singleton browser drivers reused across agents.

## 3. If you must see the UI: separate display contexts

If you absolutely need visible windows *and* want them not to steal focus:

- On Linux: run each browser in a different virtual framebuffer (`Xvfb`) or distinct display. Each agent’s `BrowserSession` would be configured to launch its browser pointing at a different display. This keeps their OS focus separate.
- On macOS/Windows: true non‑interfering visible automation is harder because there is one active foreground window. In practice, one of these strategies is used:
  - Accept that they run concurrently but only one has visible focus at a time.
  - Run each agent in a separate OS-level VM or container with its own desktop.
  - Use remote/headless mode + a viewer (e.g., VNC to a headless X server) per agent.

Those techniques depend on how `BrowserSession` launches the browser, which we don’t see here; you’d need to adapt at that layer.

## Reference Answer
A feature has been added to the browser-use library that supports configuring a custom Chrome remote debugging port. This feature enables running multiple browser agents simultaneously with the same Chrome binary but on different ports, and also allows launching user-provided Chrome without closing existing Chrome instances.

The technique is to pass your own `browser_binary_path` + different debug ports in each agent's `BrowserConfig`, e.g.

- `BrowserConfig(..., browser_binary_path='...', chrome_remote_debugging_port=9222)`
- `BrowserConfig(..., browser_binary_path='...', chrome_remote_debugging_port=9223)`
- `BrowserConfig(..., browser_binary_path='...', chrome_remote_debugging_port=9224)`
- `BrowserConfig(..., browser_binary_path='...', chrome_remote_debugging_port=9225)`

This should allow you to run multiple agents in parallel without them interfering with each other. This feature is on `main` but not yet released, so to use it you have to: `uv pip install -U git+https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use.git@main`
